preamble: In Standard Chinese the mid vowel phoneme /ə/ is realized as the back unrounded [ɤ] in an open syllable without a medial glide (歌 gē [kɤ], 喝 hē [xɤ]), as [e] after medial i or ü, as [o] after medial u, and as [ə] before -n (很 hěn [xən]), following the finals table after Duanmu (2000) and Lin (2007). The [ɤ] allophone is pronounced as a sequence [ɰɤ̞].

examples.from: 歌 gē 'song', /ə/ in an open syllable
喝 hē 'to drink', /ə/ in an open syllable
examples.note: Before -n the same phoneme is [ə]: 很 hěn [xən²¹⁴].

examples.from: 車 chē 'vehicle', /ə/ in an open syllable

languageExamples.context: Open syllable without a medial glide
